answer: Agents secure entry by performing 1,000 unique verified-work model-repair cycles, a cost honest nodes pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A global verifier acts as a mirror to monitor task registries for identity redundancy. If a node attempts to signal memory to a clone, it leaves a faint thread of evidence across the data-shard. We assume nodes maintain a ferrous-stable record of their own computational trace. Any leakage detected during these repairs triggers a permanent identity burn. The protocol assumes audit logs remain non-colluding.
